newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Sabena sees deal with unions next week.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Sabena sees deal with unions next week.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena said on Friday that key talks with trade unions on a 4.7 billion belgian franc ($149.7 million) plan aimed at restoring the company to profitability from 1998 should be finalised next week.

"There is progress. Everything has not been decided yet (but) the agreements are being prepared... I believe everything will finish on October 31, that's still the target (date)," Sabena spokesman Eric Platteau told Reuters.
Sabena, owned 49.5 percent by Swissair, has been negotiating with unions since mid-June on chief executive Paul Reutlinger's 'Horizon 98' savings plan.

Management will account for 2.7 billion francs in savings. The remainder has to come from labour-related cost reductions and are sought through a combination of job cuts, staff flexibility and wage cuts.
A deal on job cuts was reached mid-September and was based on early retirement for 470 people, voluntary redundancies, part-time work, holidays without pay and internal transfers.
"Now a decision is being taken on flexibility and (a deal) should be signed soon," Platteau said.
"Once that's happened, there's only the stage of wage cuts that is left. But if the two billion can be found from flexibility and other measures, there will be no third stage," he said.
